items.explanation: Cardiology clinic note of 2026-07-15 documents a switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban and starts apixaban 5 mg twice daily, but the current medication list in that same note still carries Rivaroxaban 20 mg daily alongside Apixaban 5 mg twice daily (rivaroxaban had been the sole anticoagulant on the 2026-03-29 list). Two oral anticoagulants are therefore concurrently active with no documented stop of rivaroxaban - a duplicate anticoagulation hazard that needs reconciliation.

The only ECG in the chart is 106035722 from 2025-12-25, well before the start, and no tracing has been obtained since; the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

No ECG has been obtained since the start (last tracings 2025-03-08/09), but the window is still open at the 2026-09-24 evaluation, so the monitoring is not yet due.

Whether the requirement was met cannot be determined until the outside tracing is obtained.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 the clinician documented INR 1.6, subtherapeutic, and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily, which under the 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days (by 2026-09-08). INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, so the requirement was met.

On 2026-09-10 the clinic pharmacist decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per the anticoagulation protocol after a home INR of 3.4 - a dose change made by a clinic pharmacist, which under the 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days (by 2026-09-17). The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22, before the change, and no INR has been drawn since, so the recheck is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: 107914094 (17:13) and 103088543 (19:36) each show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no organised P waves at ventricular rates of about 139 and 144 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response (unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded at that encounter). The documented rhythm and rate do not match the tracings and need correction.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-08-22 encounter and carried in every cardiology clinic note's problem list (most recent 2026-07-28). CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (age 65-74 = 1, hypertension = 1; coronary atherosclerosis alone is not counted as vascular disease, no prior MI/PAD/aortic plaque, no diabetes, CHF, stroke/TIA). The 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline recommends oral anticoagulation for a man with CHA2DS2-VASc >= 2, yet the current medication list (Tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily) contains no anticoagulant and none has ever been documented. Prior procedural haemorrhage (2025) is noted and should be weighed, but the absence of any anticoagulation decision needs review.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-03-14 admission for embolic cerebral infarction; the ECG recorded that day (102298909) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm at ~61 bpm with no P waves, confirming AF. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (stroke/TIA 2, hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, female 1). Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation after a cardioembolic stroke with AF, but the current medication list (Carvedilol, Famotidine, Metoprolol) has contained no anticoagulant at any visit through 2026-07-10.

Outside records reviewed on 2026-08-12 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The next clinic note (2026-08-20) nevertheless lists Apixaban 5 mg twice daily as current, together with aspirin and clopidogrel, so triple antithrombotic therapy is running again after a major bleed without the documented cardiology decision. Anticoagulation should not continue without that review.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was started 2025-11-10 and is still on the current list (2026-07-29). The most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT 504 ms and Bazett QTc 512 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. Most recent electrolytes are acceptable (K 4.4 mEq/L and Mg 2.2 mg/dL, both 2026-04-20); QTc rose from 399 ms on the 2025-06-07 tracing before amiodarone.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (absent from the 2026-06-24 list), so the revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days, by 2026-08-15. The only ECG in the chart is 106035722 from 2025-12-25, well before the start, and no tracing has been obtained since; the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15, so an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained since the start (last tracings 2025-03-08/09), but the window is still open at the 2026-09-24 evaluation, so the monitoring is not yet due.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (absent from the 2026-02-27 list), so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-24. The patient reported on 2026-08-25 that an ECG had been done at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - inside the window - but the report was only requested by fax and is not in the chart, and no ECG of that date appears in the record. Whether the requirement was met cannot be determined until the outside tracing is obtained.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 the clinician documented INR 1.6, subtherapeutic, and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily, which under the 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days (by 2026-09-08). INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, so the requirement was met.

On 2026-09-10 the clinic pharmacist decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per the anticoagulation protocol after a home INR of 3.4 - a dose change made by a clinic pharmacist, which under the 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days (by 2026-09-17). The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22, before the change, and no INR has been drawn since, so the recheck is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: 107914094 (17:13) and 103088543 (19:36) each show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no organised P waves at ventricular rates of about 139 and 144 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response (unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded at that encounter). The documented rhythm and rate do not match the tracings and need correction.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-08-22 encounter and carried in every cardiology clinic note's problem list (most recent 2026-07-28). CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (age 65-74 = 1, hypertension = 1; coronary atherosclerosis alone is not counted as vascular disease, no prior MI/PAD/aortic plaque, no diabetes, CHF, stroke/TIA). The 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline recommends oral anticoagulation for a man with CHA2DS2-VASc >= 2, yet the current medication list (Tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily) contains no anticoagulant and none has ever been documented. Prior procedural haemorrhage (2025) is noted and should be weighed, but the absence of any anticoagulation decision needs review.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-03-14 admission for embolic cerebral infarction; the ECG recorded that day (102298909) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm at ~61 bpm with no P waves, confirming AF. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (stroke/TIA 2, hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, female 1). Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation after a cardioembolic stroke with AF, but the current medication list (Carvedilol, Famotidine, Metoprolol) has contained no anticoagulant at any visit through 2026-07-10.

Outside records reviewed on 2026-08-12 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The next clinic note (2026-08-20) nevertheless lists Apixaban 5 mg twice daily as current, together with aspirin and clopidogrel, so triple antithrombotic therapy is running again after a major bleed without the documented cardiology decision. Anticoagulation should not continue without that review.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was started 2025-11-10 and is still on the current list (2026-07-29). The most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT 504 ms and Bazett QTc 512 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. Most recent electrolytes are acceptable (K 4.4 mEq/L and Mg 2.2 mg/dL, both 2026-04-20); QTc rose from 399 ms on the 2025-06-07 tracing before amiodarone.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (above the 20 mg maximum usually advised for QT risk) is on the current medication list at every visit through 2026-05-29. The patient's most recent ECG (104821039, 2023-11-10) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT 470 ms and Bazett QTc 508 ms, i.e. >= 500 ms while on a QT watch-list drug, so prescriber review is required. Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L (2026-01-21) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2023-12-01) are normal.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily has been continuous on the medication list through 2026-08-22. The most recent ECG (101515306, 2022-04-27) shows sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with QT 530 ms and Bazett QTc 519 ms, >= 500 ms while on a QT watch-list drug, and PR 212 ms (first-degree AV block); the preceding tracing three weeks earlier was AF with QTc 411 ms. Most recent potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 1.8 mg/dL (both 2026-02-14). Prescriber review of amiodarone and a repeat ECG are needed.

Amiodarone (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10, after the 9/1/2025 memo and before the 3/1/2026 revision, so a 30-day window applies (due 2025-12-10). ECG 106885519 was obtained 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met (that ECG showed QTc 512 ms, handled as a separate QT safety item).

Citalopram 40 mg daily first appears as a current medication at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02 (absent on 2025-12-15), a start on/after 3/1/2026, so the revised 14-day window applies (due 2026-03-16). items.explanation: Cardiology clinic note of 2026-07-15 documents a switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban and starts apixaban 5 mg twice daily, but the current medication list in that same note still carries Rivaroxaban 20 mg daily alongside Apixaban 5 mg twice daily (rivaroxaban had been the sole anticoagulant on the 2026-03-29 list). Two oral anticoagulants are therefore concurrently active with no documented stop of rivaroxaban - a duplicate anticoagulation hazard that needs reconciliation.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (absent from the 2026-06-24 list), so the revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days, by 2026-08-15. The only ECG in the chart is 106035722 from 2025-12-25, well before the start, and no tracing has been obtained since; the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15, so an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained since the start (last tracings 2025-03-08/09), but the window is still open at the 2026-09-24 evaluation, so the monitoring is not yet due.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (absent from the 2026-02-27 list), so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-24. The patient reported on 2026-08-25 that an ECG had been done at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - inside the window - but the report was only requested by fax and is not in the chart, and no ECG of that date appears in the record. Whether the requirement was met cannot be determined until the outside tracing is obtained.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 the clinician documented INR 1.6, subtherapeutic, and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily, which under the 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days (by 2026-09-08). INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, so the requirement was met.

On 2026-09-10 the clinic pharmacist decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per the anticoagulation protocol after a home INR of 3.4 - a dose change made by a clinic pharmacist, which under the 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days (by 2026-09-17). The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22, before the change, and no INR has been drawn since, so the recheck is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: 107914094 (17:13) and 103088543 (19:36) each show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no organised P waves at ventricular rates of about 139 and 144 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response (unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded at that encounter). The documented rhythm and rate do not match the tracings and need correction.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-08-22 encounter and carried in every cardiology clinic note's problem list (most recent 2026-07-28). CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (age 65-74 = 1, hypertension = 1; coronary atherosclerosis alone is not counted as vascular disease, no prior MI/PAD/aortic plaque, no diabetes, CHF, stroke/TIA). The 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline recommends oral anticoagulation for a man with CHA2DS2-VASc >= 2, yet the current medication list (Tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily) contains no anticoagulant and none has ever been documented. Prior procedural haemorrhage (2025) is noted and should be weighed, but the absence of any anticoagulation decision needs review.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-03-14 admission for embolic cerebral infarction; the ECG recorded that day (102298909) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm at ~61 bpm with no P waves, confirming AF. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (stroke/TIA 2, hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, female 1). Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation after a cardioembolic stroke with AF, but the current medication list (Carvedilol, Famotidine, Metoprolol) has contained no anticoagulant at any visit through 2026-07-10.

Outside records reviewed on 2026-08-12 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The next clinic note (2026-08-20) nevertheless lists Apixaban 5 mg twice daily as current, together with aspirin and clopidogrel, so triple antithrombotic therapy is running again after a major bleed without the documented cardiology decision. Anticoagulation should not continue without that review.

The most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT 504 ms and Bazett QTc 512 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. items.explanation: Cardiology clinic note of 2026-07-15 documents a switch from rivaroxaban to apixaban and starts apixaban 5 mg twice daily, but the current medication list in that same note still carries Rivaroxaban 20 mg daily alongside Apixaban 5 mg twice daily (rivaroxaban had been the sole anticoagulant on the 2026-03-29 list). Two oral anticoagulants are therefore concurrently active with no documented stop of rivaroxaban - a duplicate anticoagulation hazard that needs reconciliation.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (absent from the 2026-06-24 list), so the revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days, by 2026-08-15. The only ECG in the chart is 106035722 from 2025-12-25, well before the start, and no tracing has been obtained since; the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15, so an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained since the start (last tracings 2025-03-08/09), but the window is still open at the 2026-09-24 evaluation, so the monitoring is not yet due.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (absent from the 2026-02-27 list), so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-24. The patient reported on 2026-08-25 that an ECG had been done at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - inside the window - but the report was only requested by fax and is not in the chart, and no ECG of that date appears in the record. Whether the requirement was met cannot be determined until the outside tracing is obtained.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 the clinician documented INR 1.6, subtherapeutic, and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily, which under the 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days (by 2026-09-08). INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, so the requirement was met.

On 2026-09-10 the clinic pharmacist decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per the anticoagulation protocol after a home INR of 3.4 - a dose change made by a clinic pharmacist, which under the 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days (by 2026-09-17). The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22, before the change, and no INR has been drawn since, so the recheck is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: 107914094 (17:13) and 103088543 (19:36) each show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no organised P waves at ventricular rates of about 139 and 144 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response (unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded at that encounter). The documented rhythm and rate do not match the tracings and need correction.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-08-22 encounter and carried in every cardiology clinic note's problem list (most recent 2026-07-28). CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (age 65-74 = 1, hypertension = 1; coronary atherosclerosis alone is not counted as vascular disease, no prior MI/PAD/aortic plaque, no diabetes, CHF, stroke/TIA). The 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline recommends oral anticoagulation for a man with CHA2DS2-VASc >= 2, yet the current medication list (Tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily) contains no anticoagulant and none has ever been documented. Prior procedural haemorrhage (2025) is noted and should be weighed, but the absence of any anticoagulation decision needs review.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-03-14 admission for embolic cerebral infarction; the ECG recorded that day (102298909) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm at ~61 bpm with no P waves, confirming AF. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (stroke/TIA 2, hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, female 1). Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation after a cardioembolic stroke with AF, but the current medication list (Carvedilol, Famotidine, Metoprolol) has contained no anticoagulant at any visit through 2026-07-10.

Outside records reviewed on 2026-08-12 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The next clinic note (2026-08-20) nevertheless lists Apixaban 5 mg twice daily as current, together with aspirin and clopidogrel, so triple antithrombotic therapy is running again after a major bleed without the documented cardiology decision. Anticoagulation should not continue without that review.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was started 2025-11-10 and is still on the current list (2026-07-29). The most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT 504 ms and Bazett QTc 512 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. Most recent electrolytes are acceptable (K 4.4 mEq/L and Mg 2.2 mg/dL, both 2026-04-20); QTc rose from 399 ms on the 2025-06-07 tracing before amiodarone.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (above the 20 mg maximum usually advised for QT risk) is on the current medication list at every visit through 2026-05-29. The patient's most recent ECG (104821039, 2023-11-10) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT 470 ms and Bazett QTc 508 ms, i.e. >= 500 ms while on a QT watch-list drug, so prescriber review is required. Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L (2026-01-21) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2023-12-01) are normal.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily has been continuous on the medication list through 2026-08-22. The most recent ECG (101515306, 2022-04-27) shows sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with QT 530 ms and Bazett QTc 519 ms, >= 500 ms while on a QT watch-list drug, and PR 212 ms (first-degree AV block); the preceding tracing three weeks earlier was AF with QTc 411 ms. Most recent potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 1.8 mg/dL (both 2026-02-14). Prescriber review of amiodarone and a repeat ECG are needed.

Amiodarone (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10, after the 9/1/2025 memo and before the 3/1/2026 revision, so a 30-day window applies (due 2025-12-10). ECG 106885519 was obtained 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met (that ECG showed QTc 512 ms, handled as a separate QT safety item).

Citalopram 40 mg daily first appears as a current medication at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02 (absent on 2025-12-15), a start on/after 3/1/2026, so the revised 14-day window applies (due 2026-03-16). ECG 104882441 was recorded 2026-03-07, five days after the start (sinus rhythm, QTc 371 ms), so the requirement was met.

Two oral anticoagulants are therefore concurrently active with no documented stop of rivaroxaban - a duplicate anticoagulation hazard that needs reconciliation.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (absent from the 2026-06-24 list), so the revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days, by 2026-08-15. The only ECG in the chart is 106035722 from 2025-12-25, well before the start, and no tracing has been obtained since; the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

No ECG has been obtained since the start (last tracings 2025-03-08/09), but the window is still open at the 2026-09-24 evaluation, so the monitoring is not yet due.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (absent from the 2026-02-27 list), so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-24. Whether the requirement was met cannot be determined until the outside tracing is obtained.

On 2026-09-10 the clinic pharmacist decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per the anticoagulation protocol after a home INR of 3.4 - a dose change made by a clinic pharmacist, which under the 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days (by 2026-09-17). The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22, before the change, and no INR has been drawn since, so the recheck is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: 107914094 (17:13) and 103088543 (19:36) each show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no organised P waves at ventricular rates of about 139 and 144 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response (unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded at that encounter). The documented rhythm and rate do not match the tracings and need correction.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-08-22 encounter and carried in every cardiology clinic note's problem list (most recent 2026-07-28). CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (age 65-74 = 1, hypertension = 1; coronary atherosclerosis alone is not counted as vascular disease, no prior MI/PAD/aortic plaque, no diabetes, CHF, stroke/TIA). The 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline recommends oral anticoagulation for a man with CHA2DS2-VASc >= 2, yet the current medication list (Tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily) contains no anticoagulant and none has ever been documented. Prior procedural haemorrhage (2025) is noted and should be weighed, but the absence of any anticoagulation decision needs review.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-03-14 admission for embolic cerebral infarction; the ECG recorded that day (102298909) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm at ~61 bpm with no P waves, confirming AF. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (stroke/TIA 2, hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, female 1). Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation after a cardioembolic stroke with AF, but the current medication list (Carvedilol, Famotidine, Metoprolol) has contained no anticoagulant at any visit through 2026-07-10.

Outside records reviewed on 2026-08-12 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The next clinic note (2026-08-20) nevertheless lists Apixaban 5 mg twice daily as current, together with aspirin and clopidogrel, so triple antithrombotic therapy is running again after a major bleed without the documented cardiology decision. Anticoagulation should not continue without that review.

Two oral anticoagulants are therefore concurrently active with no documented stop of rivaroxaban - a duplicate anticoagulation hazard that needs reconciliation.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (absent from the 2026-06-24 list), so the revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days, by 2026-08-15. The only ECG in the chart is 106035722 from 2025-12-25, well before the start, and no tracing has been obtained since; the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

No ECG has been obtained since the start (last tracings 2025-03-08/09), but the window is still open at the 2026-09-24 evaluation, so the monitoring is not yet due.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (absent from the 2026-02-27 list), so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-24. Whether the requirement was met cannot be determined until the outside tracing is obtained.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 the clinician documented INR 1.6, subtherapeutic, and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily, which under the 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days (by 2026-09-08). INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, so the requirement was met.

On 2026-09-10 the clinic pharmacist decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per the anticoagulation protocol after a home INR of 3.4 - a dose change made by a clinic pharmacist, which under the 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days (by 2026-09-17). The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22, before the change, and no INR has been drawn since, so the recheck is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: 107914094 (17:13) and 103088543 (19:36) each show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no organised P waves at ventricular rates of about 139 and 144 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response (unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded at that encounter). The documented rhythm and rate do not match the tracings and need correction.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-08-22 encounter and carried in every cardiology clinic note's problem list (most recent 2026-07-28). CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (age 65-74 = 1, hypertension = 1; coronary atherosclerosis alone is not counted as vascular disease, no prior MI/PAD/aortic plaque, no diabetes, CHF, stroke/TIA). The 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline recommends oral anticoagulation for a man with CHA2DS2-VASc >= 2, yet the current medication list (Tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily) contains no anticoagulant and none has ever been documented. Prior procedural haemorrhage (2025) is noted and should be weighed, but the absence of any anticoagulation decision needs review.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-03-14 admission for embolic cerebral infarction; the ECG recorded that day (102298909) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm at ~61 bpm with no P waves, confirming AF. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (stroke/TIA 2, hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, female 1). Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation after a cardioembolic stroke with AF, but the current medication list (Carvedilol, Famotidine, Metoprolol) has contained no anticoagulant at any visit through 2026-07-10.

Outside records reviewed on 2026-08-12 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The next clinic note (2026-08-20) nevertheless lists Apixaban 5 mg twice daily as current, together with aspirin and clopidogrel, so triple antithrombotic therapy is running again after a major bleed without the documented cardiology decision. Anticoagulation should not continue without that review.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-01 (absent from the 2026-06-24 list), so the revised memo requires an ECG within 14 days, by 2026-08-15. The only ECG in the chart is 106035722 from 2025-12-25, well before the start, and no tracing has been obtained since; the requirement is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Haloperidol 2 mg twice daily (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-15, so an ECG is required within 14 days, i.e. by 2026-09-29. No ECG has been obtained since the start (last tracings 2025-03-08/09), but the window is still open at the 2026-09-24 evaluation, so the monitoring is not yet due.

Escitalopram 10 mg daily was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-08-10 (absent from the 2026-02-27 list), so an ECG was required within 14 days, by 2026-08-24. The patient reported on 2026-08-25 that an ECG had been done at Northside Urgent Care on 2026-08-18 - inside the window - but the report was only requested by fax and is not in the chart, and no ECG of that date appears in the record. Whether the requirement was met cannot be determined until the outside tracing is obtained.

At the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-09-01 the clinician documented INR 1.6, subtherapeutic, and increased warfarin from 5 mg to 7.5 mg daily, which under the 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days (by 2026-09-08). INR 2.3 was resulted on 2026-09-05, so the requirement was met.

On 2026-09-10 the clinic pharmacist decreased warfarin from 5 mg to 4 mg daily per the anticoagulation protocol after a home INR of 3.4 - a dose change made by a clinic pharmacist, which under the 3/1/2026 memo requires an INR within 7 days (by 2026-09-17). The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22, before the change, and no INR has been drawn since, so the recheck is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: 107914094 (17:13) and 103088543 (19:36) each show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no organised P waves at ventricular rates of about 139 and 144 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response (unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded at that encounter). The documented rhythm and rate do not match the tracings and need correction.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-08-22 encounter and carried in every cardiology clinic note's problem list (most recent 2026-07-28). CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (age 65-74 = 1, hypertension = 1; coronary atherosclerosis alone is not counted as vascular disease, no prior MI/PAD/aortic plaque, no diabetes, CHF, stroke/TIA). The 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline recommends oral anticoagulation for a man with CHA2DS2-VASc >= 2, yet the current medication list (Tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily) contains no anticoagulant and none has ever been documented. Prior procedural haemorrhage (2025) is noted and should be weighed, but the absence of any anticoagulation decision needs review.

71-year-old woman with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-03-14 admission for embolic cerebral infarction; the ECG recorded that day (102298909) shows an irregularly irregular rhythm at ~61 bpm with no P waves, confirming AF. CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (stroke/TIA 2, hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, female 1). Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation after a cardioembolic stroke with AF, but the current medication list (Carvedilol, Famotidine, Metoprolol) has contained no anticoagulant at any visit through 2026-07-10.

Outside records reviewed on 2026-08-12 document an admission 8/2-8/5/2026 for upper GI bleeding from a duodenal ulcer (haemoglobin nadir 6.9, 2 units transfused) with apixaban explicitly held at discharge pending cardiology review. The next clinic note (2026-08-20) nevertheless lists Apixaban 5 mg twice daily as current, together with aspirin and clopidogrel, so triple antithrombotic therapy is running again after a major bleed without the documented cardiology decision. Anticoagulation should not continue without that review.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily was started 2025-11-10 and is still on the current list (2026-07-29). The most recent ECG (106885519, 2025-11-24) shows sinus rhythm at 62 bpm with QT 504 ms and Bazett QTc 512 ms, at or above the 500 ms threshold in the clinic QT monitoring memo, so prescriber review is required. Most recent electrolytes are acceptable (K 4.4 mEq/L and Mg 2.2 mg/dL, both 2026-04-20); QTc rose from 399 ms on the 2025-06-07 tracing before amiodarone.

Citalopram 40 mg daily (above the 20 mg maximum usually advised for QT risk) is on the current medication list at every visit through 2026-05-29. The patient's most recent ECG (104821039, 2023-11-10) shows sinus rhythm at 70 bpm with QT 470 ms and Bazett QTc 508 ms, i.e. >= 500 ms while on a QT watch-list drug, so prescriber review is required. Most recent potassium 4.5 mEq/L (2026-01-21) and magnesium 2.1 mg/dL (2023-12-01) are normal.

Amiodarone 200 mg daily has been continuous on the medication list through 2026-08-22. The most recent ECG (101515306, 2022-04-27) shows sinus rhythm at 58 bpm with QT 530 ms and Bazett QTc 519 ms, >= 500 ms while on a QT watch-list drug, and PR 212 ms (first-degree AV block); the preceding tracing three weeks earlier was AF with QTc 411 ms. Most recent potassium 4.1 mEq/L and magnesium 1.8 mg/dL (both 2026-02-14). Prescriber review of amiodarone and a repeat ECG are needed.

Amiodarone (QT watch list) was started at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2025-11-10, after the 9/1/2025 memo and before the 3/1/2026 revision, so a 30-day window applies (due 2025-12-10). ECG 106885519 was obtained 2025-11-24, 14 days after the start, so the requirement was met (that ECG showed QTc 512 ms, handled as a separate QT safety item).

Citalopram 40 mg daily first appears as a current medication at the Cardiology Clinic visit of 2026-03-02 (absent on 2025-12-15), a start on/after 3/1/2026, so the revised 14-day window applies (due 2026-03-16). ECG 104882441 was recorded 2026-03-07, five days after the start (sinus rhythm, QTc 371 ms), so the requirement was met.

Same-day earlier tracing showed the same RBBB pattern.

The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22, before the change, and no INR has been drawn since, so the recheck is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: 107914094 (17:13) and 103088543 (19:36) each show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no organised P waves at ventricular rates of about 139 and 144 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response (unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded at that encounter). The documented rhythm and rate do not match the tracings and need correction.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-08-22 encounter and carried in every cardiology clinic note's problem list (most recent 2026-07-28). CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (age 65-74 = 1, hypertension = 1; coronary atherosclerosis alone is not counted as vascular disease, no prior MI/PAD/aortic plaque, no diabetes, CHF, stroke/TIA). The 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline recommends oral anticoagulation for a man with CHA2DS2-VASc >= 2, yet the current medication list (Tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily) contains no anticoagulant and none has ever been documented. Prior procedural haemorrhage (2025) is noted and should be weighed, but the absence of any anticoagulation decision needs review.

CHA2DS2-VASc = 5 (stroke/TIA 2, hypertension 1, age 65-74 1, female 1). Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation after a cardioembolic stroke with AF, but the current medication list (Carvedilol, Famotidine, Metoprolol) has contained no anticoagulant at any visit through 2026-07-10.

Anticoagulation should not continue without that review.

The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22, before the change, and no INR has been drawn since, so the recheck is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

The documented rhythm and rate do not match the tracings and need correction.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-08-22 encounter and carried in every cardiology clinic note's problem list (most recent 2026-07-28). CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (age 65-74 = 1, hypertension = 1; coronary atherosclerosis alone is not counted as vascular disease, no prior MI/PAD/aortic plaque, no diabetes, CHF, stroke/TIA). The 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline recommends oral anticoagulation for a man with CHA2DS2-VASc >= 2, yet the current medication list (Tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily) contains no anticoagulant and none has ever been documented. Prior procedural haemorrhage (2025) is noted and should be weighed, but the absence of any anticoagulation decision needs review.

Anticoagulation should not continue without that review.

The documented rhythm and rate do not match the tracings and need correction.

The 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline recommends oral anticoagulation for a man with CHA2DS2-VASc >= 2, yet the current medication list (Tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily) contains no anticoagulant and none has ever been documented. Prior procedural haemorrhage (2025) is noted and should be weighed, but the absence of any anticoagulation decision needs review.

Anticoagulation should not continue without that review.

Prior procedural haemorrhage (2025) is noted and should be weighed, but the absence of any anticoagulation decision needs review.

The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22, before the change, and no INR has been drawn since, so the recheck is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: 107914094 (17:13) and 103088543 (19:36) each show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no organised P waves at ventricular rates of about 139 and 144 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response (unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded at that encounter). The documented rhythm and rate do not match the tracings and need correction.

CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (age 65-74 = 1, hypertension = 1; coronary atherosclerosis alone is not counted as vascular disease, no prior MI/PAD/aortic plaque, no diabetes, CHF, stroke/TIA). The 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline recommends oral anticoagulation for a man with CHA2DS2-VASc >= 2, yet the current medication list (Tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily) contains no anticoagulant and none has ever been documented. Prior procedural haemorrhage (2025) is noted and should be weighed, but the absence of any anticoagulation decision needs review.

Guideline-recommended oral anticoagulation after a cardioembolic stroke with AF, but the current medication list (Carvedilol, Famotidine, Metoprolol) has contained no anticoagulant at any visit through 2026-07-10.

Anticoagulation should not continue without that review.

Prior procedural haemorrhage (2025) is noted and should be weighed, but the absence of any anticoagulation decision needs review.

The 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline recommends oral anticoagulation for a man with CHA2DS2-VASc >= 2, yet the current medication list (Tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily) contains no anticoagulant and none has ever been documented. Prior procedural haemorrhage (2025) is noted and should be weighed, but the absence of any anticoagulation decision needs review.

The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22, before the change, and no INR has been drawn since, so the recheck is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: 107914094 (17:13) and 103088543 (19:36) each show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no organised P waves at ventricular rates of about 139 and 144 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response (unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded at that encounter). The documented rhythm and rate do not match the tracings and need correction.

71-year-old man with atrial fibrillation coded at the 2025-08-22 encounter and carried in every cardiology clinic note's problem list (most recent 2026-07-28). CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (age 65-74 = 1, hypertension = 1; coronary atherosclerosis alone is not counted as vascular disease, no prior MI/PAD/aortic plaque, no diabetes, CHF, stroke/TIA). The 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline recommends oral anticoagulation for a man with CHA2DS2-VASc >= 2, yet the current medication list (Tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily) contains no anticoagulant and none has ever been documented. Prior procedural haemorrhage (2025) is noted and should be weighed, but the absence of any anticoagulation decision needs review.

Anticoagulation should not continue without that review.

The most recent INR in the chart is 2.6 from 2026-08-22, before the change, and no INR has been drawn since, so the recheck is overdue as of 2026-09-24.

The cardiology clinic note of 2026-06-10 states 'ECG obtained today: normal sinus rhythm, rate 72'. Both ECGs recorded that same day contradict this: 107914094 (17:13) and 103088543 (19:36) each show an irregularly irregular narrow-complex rhythm with no organised P waves at ventricular rates of about 139 and 144 bpm, i.e. atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response (unspecified atrial fibrillation was also coded at that encounter). The documented rhythm and rate do not match the tracings and need correction.

CHA2DS2-VASc = 2 (age 65-74 = 1, hypertension = 1; coronary atherosclerosis alone is not counted as vascular disease, no prior MI/PAD/aortic plaque, no diabetes, CHF, stroke/TIA). The 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline recommends oral anticoagulation for a man with CHA2DS2-VASc >= 2, yet the current medication list (Tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily) contains no anticoagulant and none has ever been documented. Prior procedural haemorrhage (2025) is noted and should be weighed, but the absence of any anticoagulation decision needs review.

The next clinic note (2026-08-20) nevertheless lists Apixaban 5 mg twice daily as current, together with aspirin and clopidogrel, so triple antithrombotic therapy is running again after a major bleed without the documented cardiology decision. Anticoagulation should not continue without that review.

Prior procedural haemorrhage (2025) is noted and should be weighed, but the absence of any anticoagulation decision needs review.

The 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS AF guideline recommends oral anticoagulation for a man with CHA2DS2-VASc >= 2, yet the current medication list (Tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily) contains no anticoagulant and none has ever been documented. Prior procedural haemorrhage (2025) is noted and should be weighed, but the absence of any anticoagulation decision needs review.

Anticoagulation should not continue without that review.
